problem: Navigation agents either need per-environment SLAM/exploration or extensive training in the same layout; they do not exploit a given rough abstract 2-D map to navigate a novel 3-D maze zero-shot, because the map-to-world state/action correspondence is unknown.
motivation: Like a tourist reading a paper map, an agent should follow a rough given solution in a novel layout without exploring or training. Explicit localization and planning on the map image is brittle because map cells and agent poses/actions differ in scale and nature, and maps and localization are noisy.
key_idea: Use a task-conditioned hypermodel that maps the abstract map and start/goal to the weights of a latent transition model in a MuZero-style planner, trained with n-step hindsight goal relabelling and an auxiliary model loss, so planning happens in the agent's own action space.
insight: Conditioning the transition-model weights (not the state) on the map lets the model reuse local map patterns and generalize compositionally from only 20 training maps. Model-based planning with the learned model beats the map-conditioned model-free Ape-X HER DQN, especially at long distance (hierarchical SR 0.80 vs 0.45), and is robust to noisy maps and localization compared with a deterministic planner. Robustness ablations show graceful degradation under map flips, perspective distortion and position noise (though no ablation of the hypermodel itself or HER is reported in the text).
method: Task-conditioned hypermodel: a meta-network h_psi maps context c=(downsampled global map, cropped local map, one-hot start, one-hot goal) to weights phi of the latent transition network f_phi(s,a)->(s',r)

MuZero-style planning: encoder e_theta maps the 12-D state to latent; MCTS runs with the hypermodel-generated dynamics; a task-conditioned prediction net g_theta(s,c) gives policy and value; actions stay in the original action space
n-step hindsight goal relabelling: relabel failed goals with future visited positions, recompute rewards, termination and bootstrapped task-conditioned values for n-step targets

Auxiliary model loss: predict next latent states/rewards from the map-conditioned hypermodel (variational mutual-information bound between context and predicted trajectory); the total loss is the sum of task and model losses over K steps
Hierarchical navigation: a landmark oracle gives subgoals at fixed distance (5) along the shortest map path, fed sequentially as local start-goal pairs
Baselines: MMN-MF (map-conditioned Ape-X HER DQN, single-step HER), single-task DQN (no context) and Random

setting.backbone: MuZero-style MCTS with a HyperNetwork transition model (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: RL in DeepMind Lab on 20 generated maps per map size (13x13 to 21x21), start-goal pairs with distance 1-5, random per episode; no extra data
setting.observation: abstract 2-D occupancy map + one-hot start/goal indicators + 12-D joint state vector (position, orientation, velocities) + reward; no visual input
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward, backward, strafe left/right, look left/right (action repeat 10)
setting.privileged: Given abstract map with start/goal; ground-truth agent position/pose state; landmark oracle for hierarchical navigation

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 unseen 13x13 maps; global start top-right, goal bottom-left; landmark distance 5
numbers.extra: landmark oracle subgoals; trained on 20 maps with distance<=5
numbers.evidence: Table 1, landmark distance 5: SPL 0.63, SR 0.80 (16 of 20 goals reached)

numbers_note: Local navigation results are in figures only (no exact values). SPL in the hierarchical table is printed on a 0-1 scale (0.61, 0.59, 0.68, 0.45, 0.63 for distances 1-5); SR converted from printed 0.80.
results: On unseen 13x13 mazes, MMN and the map-conditioned model-free MMN-MF both beat single-task DQN and Random at local navigation, with MMN better at long distances despite training only on distances <=5. In hierarchical navigation MMN reaches 16/20 global goals (SR 0.80, SPL 0.63) versus 0.45 SR / 0.28 SPL for MMN-MF, while DQN and Random score 0.
limitations: Toy synthetic DeepMind Lab mazes with a low-dimensional state vector, no visual observations
Needs a landmark oracle for long-range navigation and ground-truth position; performance degrades with growing map/localization noise
Weak baselines and no ablations of hypermodel or HER in the paper; local results only in figures
